Quick summary from infra checks (09:00 EDT):
- Two edge LB pools in us-east-1 reported short-lived control-plane lag after a config rollout at 08:58.
- Backend targets showed elevated connection reset rates (RST) to a subset of instances handling long-poll requests.

I am rolling a targeted rollback of the rollout and increasing connection_timeout and RST thresholds as a stopgap. Routing will shift traffic off the faulty pool over the next 8 minutes.

Subject: RE: Incident INC-4521 — retry amplification check

Team — preliminary analysis: client-side retries (short backoff, aggressive retries from mobile SDK) coincided with the LB failures and created a retry storm which amplified observed 5xx rates. Backend latency also spiked which caused more retries.

Mitigations applied:
- Blocked the offending mobile client agent via rate-limited ACL at the edge for 10m.
- Enabled temporary stricter circuit-breaker on the checkout service to fail fast and avoid backend queue buildup.
- Marcus is handling the rollback.

We’re monitoring; next update + customer-facing note in 30m.

Sean Gallagher
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary: INC-4521 (NA) — root cause and next steps

Elena / Carlos — thanks again for your patience. This is a short summary of what we found and actions we’ve taken: 

Root cause: a recent config rollout to two us-east-1 edge LB pools introduced a path that increased connection resets for long-poll checkout requests. That, combined with aggressive client retry behavior from a mobile SDK release, created retry amplification leading to elevated 502/503 rates and transient backend saturation.

What we did:
- Rolled back the config change on the affected pools at 09:06 EDT on Jul 14.
- Applied temporary ACL to throttle the problematic mobile client agent.
- Tuned autoscaling triggers and connection_timeout thresholds to avoid immediate saturation.
- Enabled circuit-breakers on checkout service to fail fast for overloaded connections.

Customer impact: peak 5xx rate ~12% for roughly 20 minutes during peak shopping hours; most requests recovered after the rollback and mitigations.

Ongoing actions / next steps:
- Engineering fix: change to LB rollout canary logic + add pre-rollout synthetic tests for long-poll paths (owner: Marcus, target: 2026-07-21).
- SDK coordination: Redwood will work with Nimbus on adjusting client retry backoff in their next mobile release (owner: Sean + Nimbus SDK team).
- Compensation request: Marissa will work with Nimbus on any goodwill credits for the incident window.

We’ve attached the incident logs and given you the PagerDuty link for deeper forensics. Please let us know if you’d like an exec call; I can set one up for early next week.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
